solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Instrument’s peg adjusted with skill once (12)

indicators.note: the letters are rearranged, as a tuning peg is adjusted

explanation.surface: A musician recalls tuning an instrument's peg with a skill they once had.
explanation.walkthrough: The ’s stands for 'is': Instrument is PEG SKILL ONCE rearranged. A peg suggests strings, but the answer has none.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a percussion instrument of tuned metal bars struck with hammers.

clue.text: Style of rap starts to generate almost overwhelming dread (7)

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters
to overwhelm is to engulf, so the outer letters wrap around the inner word

blocks.note: first letter of almost, still governed by 'starts to'

explanation.surface: A music critic says a style of rap tends to generate almost overwhelming dread.
explanation.walkthrough: The two starts sit either side of the dread, which they overwhelm.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the hip-hop genre built on street-crime themes.

clue.text: Chaps in team, number climbing on Scottish island above loch lacking depth (3-11)

indicators.note: 'in' places the chaps inside the team, the way players are in a side
in a down clue, climbing reads the letters bottom to top
in a down clue, the island sits over the loch

blocks.note: chaps = men, put inside the reversed pair
Iona is an island in the Inner Hebrides

explanation.surface: A travel note about men in a team, their numbers climbing, on a Scottish island above a shallow loch.
explanation.walkthrough: Both team and number climb together before the chaps go in. 'Lacking depth' looks as if it describes the loch, but it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A figurative sense: a flat character or argument, having length but no depth.

clue.text: King and leader of armada chat in boat (5)

indicators.note: the leader is the one at the front, so the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A king and his admiral chat in a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface puts everyone in a boat; the boat is the answer, and 'in' only joins it to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a small, narrow boat paddled with a double-bladed paddle.

clue.text: Propose an item broadcast after drama (8)

indicators.note: seed sown broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are scattered
'after' in its sense of later in sequence: the shuffled letters come later than the drama

blocks.note: Noh (also spelt No) is Japanese classical drama

explanation.surface: A programme planner proposes an item to be broadcast after a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: NO is the crossword spelling of Noh, the Japanese masked drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to put someone forward for a post or award.

clue.text: Long stretch of trip in Europe (4)

indicators.note: a stretch is a continuous run, here a run of letters lifted from the words that follow

explanation.surface: A long stretch of a trip spent in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' reads as an adjective for the stretch, but it is the verb: to long for something.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the verb: pining and longing both mean yearning for something absent.

clue.text: Destroy order, losing time after time (9)

indicators.note: to lose something is to be left without it, so the word goes on without that letter
'after' in its sense of later in sequence: the shortened word follows

blocks.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An instruction to destroy an order, losing time again and again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Time after time' is not repetition: the first time is T, dropped from DICTATE, and the second is ERA, placed in front.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: eradicate literally means to pull out by the roots, hence to wipe out.

clue.text: Impure hero, sort mistakenly made head of religious community (6,8)

indicators.note: done by mistake, so the letters are put in the wrong order

explanation.surface: An impure hero of some sort is wrongly appointed to lead a religious community.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface has a scandal about a bad appointment; the unlikely hero becomes the nun in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: The title given to the nun in charge of a convent, the religious community of the definition.

clue.text: Cross in past hour, upset, then relieved (6)

indicators.note: to upset is to knock over, so in a down clue the letters are turned upside down
'then' in its sense of next in order, so what follows is placed after

blocks.note: to go by is to go past

explanation.surface: Someone was cross an hour ago, upset, and then relieved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry, but it is the noun: a cross between two breeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the noun: offspring of two different breeds or species is called either.

clue.text: Poor knight, feeble, wanting wife (5)

indicators.note: 'wanting' in its sense of lacking, so the letter is missing

explanation.surface: A poor, feeble knight who lacks a wife.
explanation.walkthrough: Knight is N in chess, since K is taken by the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the adjective: lacking money or the necessities of life.

clue.text: Fellow attorney Conservative required (9)

blocks.note: a Tory is a member of Britain's Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A notice that a fellow attorney who is a Conservative is required.
explanation.walkthrough: DA is the American district attorney, and Tory is the everyday name for a British Conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: demanded by law or rule, with no choice about it.

clue.text: Putting arachnid in pipe? (8)

indicators.note: 'in' places one word inside the other

blocks.note: to pipe is to sing in a high voice; the arachnid goes inside

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they are putting a spider in a tobacco pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pipe' reads as a tube, but it is the verb, to sing shrilly.
explanation.definitionFit: An informal sense: 'stick it in the drawer' uses the verb to mean place.

clue.text: Reflected on hard image in code (6)

indicators.note: a reflection is a mirror image, so the letters read backwards

explanation.surface: Someone reflected on a hard-to-read image hidden in a code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reflected on' looks like 'thought about', but it splits: reflected is the reversal and on is RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a system for disguising a message by swapping its letters.

clue.text: Story from a relative omitting one gripping point (8)

indicators.note: to omit is to leave out, so the word is written without that letter
to grip is to hold tight, so the outer letters hold the inner word

blocks.note: a dot is a point, gripped by the rest

explanation.surface: A story told by a relative who leaves out one gripping point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gripping' reads as exciting, but it means holding.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a short, entertaining account of a real incident.

clue.text: Dreadful in operation, ignoring first in command (9)

indicators.note: to ignore the first is to pay it no attention, so the first letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Something dreadful in a military operation, ignoring the first in command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First in command' looks like a phrase, but 'first' belongs to the deletion and 'in' is only a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an official instruction issued by an authority.

clue.text: Holy ship’s company mostly in blue (6)

indicators.note: 'mostly' means most but not all of it, so the last letter is dropped
'in' places the shortened word inside the next

blocks.note: blue = sad, holding the shortened crew

explanation.surface: A holy ship's crew, most of them feeling blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue' is the mood, not the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: set apart for, or connected with, God or religion.

clue.text: Area guarded by soldier perhaps on border, a thing that’s abhorred (8)

indicators.note: guards stand around what they guard, so the letter is surrounded by the next word
in a down clue, the first part sits on top of the border

blocks.note: a hem is the border of cloth

explanation.surface: An area guarded by a soldier on the border, something everyone hates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soldier perhaps' signals an example: a soldier ant, not a soldier. The 'a' after the comma looks like part of the definition, but it is the last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: something utterly detested, originally a thing cursed by the Church.

clue.text: Walk out on expanse of land without water (6)

blocks.note: abandon a person or post: the verb, stressed on the second syllable
an arid region such as the Sahara: the noun, stressed on the first syllable

explanation.surface: Someone walks out on to a dry expanse of land.
explanation.walkthrough: The two senses are said differently but spelt the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: one spelling for both abandoning someone and a barren, arid region.

clue.text: Reject racket broken by seed (6)

indicators.note: something broken is split open, here to let the other word in

blocks.note: a din is a racket, split open
to seed a field is to sow it

explanation.surface: A tennis player rejects a racket after being broken by a seeded opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is all tennis: racket, broken, seed. None of it survives: the racket is noise and the seed is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to refuse to acknowledge someone as your own.

clue.text: Anxious at home with scoundrel coming into view (8)

indicators.note: 'with' means together with, so the parts are set side by side
to come into a place is to enter it, so one word enters the other

blocks.note: to be in is to be at home
to view is to see, taking in the scoundrel

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious at home as a scoundrel comes into view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming into view' reads as appearing, but it splits: 'coming into' is the container and 'view' is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: lacking confidence and uneasy.

clue.text: Dean set to work in part of London (4,3)

indicators.note: to work material is to knead it into a new shape, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: A cathedral dean is set to start a job in a part of London.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'set to work' reads as one phrase; only 'to work' is the instruction.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the traditionally working-class district east of the City of London.

clue.text: Put a stop to school hosting business account finally (6)

indicators.note: a host has guests inside, so the outer word holds the others
'finally' means at the end, so only the word's last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A school puts a stop to hosting a business account.
explanation.walkthrough: The school abbreviation is split open to host the business and the last letter of account.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to scotch a rumour is to kill it off.

clue.text: Beginners lead rest astray (8)

indicators.note: to go astray is to wander off course, so the letters wander from their order

blocks.note: the lead in a film is its star

explanation.surface: Novices lead everyone else off course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: the lead actor.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: those just beginning something, such as a race or a course.

clue.text: Bird that’s black and yellow, not caught (5)

indicators.note: 'not caught' means without caught, so that letter is removed

blocks.note: a large black bird of the crow family
the adjective used of glossy black hair

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher describes a bird with black and yellow plumage.
explanation.walkthrough: Three routes to one word: the bird, the colour, and 'yellow' in its cowardly sense, losing C, the cricket abbreviation for caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the large black bird of the crow family, whose name also serves as a colour.

clue.text: Mere share (4)

blocks.note: a mere is a small lake
the verb, as when resources are put together for common use

explanation.walkthrough: 'Mere' reads as 'only', but it is the noun: a small lake, common in English place names.
explanation.definitionFit: A double definition: a small lake, and to combine resources for common use.

clue.text: Boring sport, one followed by a few (9)

indicators.note: what follows comes after, so the next part is placed behind

blocks.note: to sport a hat is to wear it

explanation.surface: A spectator finds a sport dull, with one player followed by a few others.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sport' reads as a game, but it is the verb: to sport clothes is to have them on.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: so tedious that it wears you out.

clue.text: Weakness about love, say (5)

indicators.note: 'about' in its sense of around, so the outer word goes round the letter

blocks.note: a vice is a moral weakness, placed around O

explanation.surface: A confession of weakness about love, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' looks like 'for example', but it is the noun: to have a say.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for the noun: having a say in something is having an opinion that counts.

clue.text: Revolutionary behind lines, protected by new name, unusually polite (4-8)

indicators.note: 'behind' means at the back, so this part goes last
a protector surrounds what it shields, so the letters go inside the next word
done in an unusual way, so the letters are arranged out of their usual order

blocks.note: L = line, doubled for the plural
NEW NAME rearranged, wrapped around the lines
a Red is a revolutionary communist

explanation.surface: A revolutionary behind enemy lines, sheltered by a new identity, is unusually courteous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind lines' reads as a spy's position, but 'behind' just puts the revolutionary at the end, and the lines go inside the reshuffled NEW NAME.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: having good manners, courteous.
